issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify lectureName as a String, and the template expects students to add a lectureName attribute accordingly, but the solution defines lectureName as a LectureName object. This cross-artifact type mismatch will confuse students about the expected attribute type and the constructor/signature they should implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the lectureName type consistent across artifacts. Either change the solution to use a plain String for lectureName (remove or stop using the LectureName wrapper class), or update the problem statement and template to explicitly require a LectureName type and show how students should use it. Preferably revert the solution to String to match the UML and template.

issues.description: In the solution, getLectureName() is declared to return String but the lectureName field is a LectureName object and the getter directly returns that field. This produces a type mismatch/compile error and contradicts the expected getter behavior implied by the problem (lectureName as String).
issues.suggestedFix: Fix the getter so its return type matches the field type or vice versa. Options: (a) change the lectureName field to String in the solution and return that String; or (b) change getLectureName() to return LectureName (or return lectureName.toString()) and update the problem/template to reflect LectureName usage. Ensure signatures and types are consistent to avoid compile errors.

issues.description: The problem statement requires a constructor initializing attributes in the order specified by the UML (lectureName as a String followed by int attributes). The solution's constructor accepts a LectureName parameter as the first argument instead of a String, creating a mismatch between the expected constructor signature and the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the constructor parameter types with the UML and template. Either change the solution constructor to take a String as the first parameter (and remove the LectureName wrapper), or update the problem statement and template to require a LectureName parameter and document that change. Prefer keeping a String parameter to match the exercise description.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify the lectureName attribute as a String (lectureName: String), but the solution implementation introduces a new LectureName class and uses LectureName as the type for the same attribute and constructor parameter. This creates a cross-artifact identifier/type mismatch for the same conceptual entity (the lecture's name) and will confuse students expecting to use a String for lectureName (and to implement the constructor/getters/setters accordingly).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the representation of the lecture name consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to use a String for the lectureName attribute and constructor parameter (remove or stop using LectureName), or (B) update the problem statement/UML and template to specify LectureName as the intended type and explain the additional LectureName class. Align getter/setter signatures accordingly so the same identifier and type are used everywhere.
